what_it_does: When a neural network runs on a specialized AI chip (called a dataflow accelerator — a chip designed so data flows from one small processing unit to the next), a common bottleneck is simply moving data from memory to those units fast enough. DataMaestro is a programmable data-streaming engine that sits between the memory and the rest of the chip, handling data movement so the compute units are never left waiting. It intelligently pre-fetches data before it is needed, avoids the 'bank conflict' problem (where multiple requests try to read from the same memory bank at once, causing a traffic jam), and can reformat or compress data on the fly to reduce how much needs to be fetched in the first place. The system was prototyped on an FPGA (a reconfigurable chip used for testing hardware ideas) and also verified through chip-design simulation, showing it fits real silicon.
